articles.title: Conservatives’ more rigid thinking styles don’t seem to make them likelier than liberals to toe the party line
articles.summary: Conservatives tend to report more rigid thinking styles than liberals, but that doesn't appear to make them more likely to follow their party's lead. Across dozens of issues, both groups shifted toward their party's stance about equally.

articles.title: Physical attractiveness offers no protection for perpetrators of online misogyny
articles.summary: A recent experiment found that physical attractiveness does not protect internet trolls from judgment. When encountering online misogyny, users rely on the severity of the message itself rather than being swayed by the perpetrator's profile picture.

articles.title: A love of intense sweetness shows a surprising link to financial choices
articles.summary: People with a strong preference for intensely sweet tastes tend to choose immediate, smaller rewards over delayed ones. New research suggests this impatience is largely explained by a general aversion to risk rather than an overpowering desire for rewards.

articles.title: Researchers probe the oxytocin system for clues to functional neurological disorder
articles.summary: Researchers exploring Functional Neurological Disorder found that while genetics alone don't explain the condition, epigenetic markers and salivary oxytocin levels interact in ways that align with a patient's history of childhood trauma.

articles.title: Frontiers: A Roundtable Discussion on the I-Frame vs. S-Frame Debate
articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex? How should applied behavioral scientists navigate the financial and political influences on the work

articles.title: Drug target could block brain inflammation linked to Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s
articles.summary: Blocking a receptor called P2X7 significantly reduced inflammation in human brain tissue, revealing a potential new treatment strategy for neurological and psychiatric disorders. The discovery could help researchers repurpose existing drugs for conditions including traumatic brain injury, Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, depression, and schizophrenia.

articles.title: Training Numerical Intelligence via Auto-Diagnosis and Skill Discovery
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.03872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are becoming increasingly capable of generating scientific code, but generating code is not the same as improving the algorithms behind it. For numerical solvers, execution feedback can expose poor performance, but rarely reveals its underlying cause and how to address it. We introduce Auto-Diagnosis and Skill Discovery (ADSD), a framework that links numerical diagnosis to reusable solver self-improvement. ADSD follows a diagnosis-first paradigm that first explains why a solver performs poorly, then uses this diagnosis to guide the disc

articles.title: Comparative review of hybrid forecasting models for short-term prediction of building thermal load
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.06881v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, a comparative review of different hybrid models for short-term forecasting of building thermal demand is carried out. Particularly, the assessment tackles the comparison of data-driven models enhanced with other state-of-the-art techniques.
